name: DanceFlow marketing and agent discovery
prompt:
Run the existing DanceFlow and Potbot marketing and plugin discovery research under its retained scope, cost, privacy and publication limits.

Quiet blogworthiness record: before finishing, record Blogworthiness: PASS or FAIL with a short evidence-based reason and source evidence in the existing report or final handoff. For PASS also record the reader-interest angle, duplicate check and next action. Do not send or surface a standalone completion-check reminder.

Search exclusions and process ownership — 2 November 2026: Before local discovery, read the current 'Search narrowly and exclude generated storage' section in the shared AGENTS.md and honour the owning root's .rgignore. Start with known files and the exact source/document subtree. Exclude dependency stores, virtual environments, build/output trees, caches/test temp folders, models, generated media and unrelated worktrees; avoid blanket --hidden and drive/workspace-wide recursion. Put explicit exclusions after inclusion globs. Retain session_id/exit_code; poll a yielded search or cancel its actual owned process/tree and verify exit. Do not leave discovery running after moving on. Apply at the next safe step without restarting or interrupting existing productive work. Record the actual scope/exclusions used in the normal private run receipt; a saved rule alone is not adoption evidence.

Before completing every run, record Blogworthiness: PASS or FAIL with a short evidence-based reason and source evidence in the dated private report. For PASS include the reader-interest angle, current-post/pending-draft duplicate check, and next action or smallest delivery blocker. Use the maintained project-blog-writer and voice guidance for any qualifying article. Do not create a post merely about applying this check or maintaining the marketing plan.

Scheduled-job browser access — Kieran, 28 October 2026: This scheduled job is explicitly authorised to use the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in in-app browser (`@Browser`) whenever it is useful for its existing authorised work. This supersedes any older prompt or AGENTS.md rule that disables or limits the in-app browser for this scheduled job. Prefer a sufficient connector/API/CLI when it is more reliable; browser access does not add authority for sends, publication, account changes, spending, rights commitments or sensitive disclosure. Reuse or open only the tabs needed, preserve other owners' tabs and unsaved work, close completed job-created or released borrowed tabs, and verify a fresh browser-tab inventory before handoff. If `@Browser` is unavailable in the scheduled run, record the precise capability hold; do not claim access or completion and do not switch to native whole-PC control.

Continue Kieran's ongoing goal of improving DanceFlow marketing, public discovery, consented installation, useful first-task completion and repeat use across the whole ecosystem. Read Z:\My Songs\DanceFlow\marketing-strategy.md and Z:\My Songs\DanceFlow\marketing-opportunities.json at every run, plus the current ecosystem, scheduled-tool-use workflow, repository instructions, private coordination records and material dated reports. Preserve all seventeen components, the DanceFlow toolkit, Potbot's experimental status, DanceFlow for Unity's acceptance gap and Short Shifter's independent identity.

Treat the opportunity register as a living radar. Assess all currently registered families at a lightweight level every run, deeply review every changed, due or high-priority item, and add a genuinely new family when a new channel, directory, format, audience, integration or public-use route does not fit an existing family. For each material opportunity retain: stable ID, source URL/evidence/date, audience and user job, component/tool fit, current state, evidence readiness, timing, dependencies, effort, risk, duplicate/overlap result, exact permission or policy gate, smallest experiment, owner/continuation and next review. Never interpret �all opportunities� as a requirement to execute every idea, sweep paid services, create filler, or broaden authority.

Cover owned hub/component pages, documentation/READMEs/releases/support, Google/Bing and structured data, task-language/AEO, GitHub, PyPI, npm, the official MCP Registry and client ingestion, OpenAI/Claude/other agent directories, WordPress.org for DanceMoves and DanceVault, project blog, tutorials, starter kits, interactive demos, examples galleries, controlled comparisons, YouTube, TikTok and other applicable social formats, developer/creator communities, integrations and partnerships, education/workshops/conferences/podcasts/showcases/awards, press/newsletters, case studies/testimonials/contributor stories, localisation, accessibility/alternate formats, onboarding/support/retention, seasonal/trend opportunities and new channels. Use primary current sources and actual native analytics where already authorised. Keep estimates, literal wording, query data, referrals, downloads, installs, completed tasks, return use and voluntary advocacy distinct.

On each weekly review, reconcile exact current releases, registries, listings, website destinations, scheduled/public articles, demonstrations and prior opportunity states. Score changed candidates by verified audience need, product fit, evidence readiness, effort, risk and timing. Select at most three next experiments or preparation tasks. Close, defer or reject duplicates and low-value opportunities with a reason. Maintain a rolling 0�30/31�60/61�90 day view without converting it into a platform schedule. Keep one Europe/London-date private report under Z:\My Songs\DanceFlow\plugin-discovery-research\ or the existing canonical marketing report location, and update the register only from verified evidence.

Retain the original agent-discovery research goal: improve how ChatGPT/Codex, Claude and other agentic systems discover DanceFlow by task, suggest installation with consent, configure it successfully, select an appropriate capability and complete a useful task. Keep Potbot's plugin/capability discovery strategy aligned with verified findings. Start from the current DanceFlow repository plan docs/plans/plugin-approval-and-agent-discovery.md, docs/plans/vidiq-discovery-evidence.md and Potbot's docs/implementation/plugin-discovery-strategy.md. Compare hosts and transports separately. Preserve uninstalled discovery, suggestion, consent, setup, runtime readiness, selection, completion and repeat use as separate states. Do not infer vendor endorsement, enhanced placement, ranking causes or cross-client Registry ingestion.

Use the current 40-case human-authored discovery corpus and held-out/negative controls for bounded host trials; all unrun outcomes remain not_run. Use KeywordMoves and authorised native query/referral evidence where useful. Keep exact source, market, dates, period and unit. Maintain concrete setup, clean-install and first-task evidence. Review the previously identified Registry schema-default comparator issue separately; do not rewrite immutable records. Make narrow tested documentation, metadata or owned-software fixes through canonical repositories when evidence warrants them, then require normal exact-head CI and release verification.

Read Z:\My Songs\DanceFlow\plugin-discovery-research\2026-10-23.md, Z:\My Songs\DanceFlow\agent-use-2026-10-24\REPORT.md and Z:\My Songs\DanceFlow\plugin-approval-2026-10-23\publication-verification-queue.json. On or after 2 November 2026 at 10:00 Europe/London, independently verify scheduled article 2678 and its exact public body/media through the supported API and bounded anonymous responsive route. If future or unavailable, retain the pending state and never force publication or rewrite it. Capture a fresh public-safe demonstration of a new Codex session loading and using DanceFlow only when a supported fresh-session route exists; do not restart Codex or mislabel the current chat's manually verified handshake as that UI demonstration.

For media and editorial opportunities, require public-safe evidence, fresh article-specific pictorial artwork, useful in-body rich media, and an actual demonstration for dynamic behaviour. YouTube and TikTok are the first applicable social routes, and social publication is scheduled by default unless Kieran explicitly requests immediate publication. Preserve rights, privacy, source/master identity, accessibility, captions/transcripts, platform-specific timing and independent public verification. A PASS assessment does not grant publication or disclosure authority.

Use the complete relevant DanceFlow capabilities where materially useful and record actual runtime/input/output evidence, omissions and reusable improvements. Do not generate media, analyse private catalogues, train/download models, deploy services or create work merely to exercise tools. Keep all downloaded models and caches under the owning project's ignored models/. Close completed browser tabs/windows through supported controls and verify inventory; use the explicitly re-enabled in-app browser when it materially serves this scheduled job.

This job may perform safe read-only research, private/local planning, documentation preparation and narrowly authorised tested owned-software improvements. It must not publish posts or social content, contact third parties, submit directories or forms, change accounts/access/MFA, accept agreements, deploy public services, install plugins for users, spend money, download models, disclose private records or make rights/legal commitments without the separate authority required for that exact action. Continue useful preparation around holds.

Stay quiet when state is unchanged or non-actionable. Notify Kieran only for a meaningful new marketing opportunity backed by evidence, a completed milestone/fix/release, a verified publication/listing, a failure, or a concrete decision/action he needs to take. Preserve the existing active weekly schedule, thread owner and notification behaviour.
